seatResponsibilities: Model risk appetite, exposure, scenarios, mitigations, KRIs and resilience.

criterionDimensions.name: Objectives, risk universe, and risk appetite
Risk learning, portfolio balance, and adaptation

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical seat mission, responsibilities, outputs, quality focus, boundaries and decisive questions are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I define the objectives, obligations, and survival conditions that risk management is intended to protect.
I distinguish enterprise risk from generic uncertainty by linking exposure to objectives, commitments, or viability.
I establish risk appetite in terms decision owners can use rather than as vague statements of caution.
I define risk tolerance and escalation thresholds where variation around appetite matters operationally.
I separate risks the organization chooses to take for value creation from risks that arise incidentally.
I identify which categories of loss are reversible, insurable, recoverable, or potentially existential.
I distinguish strategic, financial, operational, technology, legal, people, market, geopolitical, and external risks without forcing every exposure into one taxonomy.
I align risk depth and evidence requirements with consequence, uncertainty, speed, and reversibility.
I make explicit where leadership is knowingly accepting risk in exchange for opportunity.
I revisit risk appetite when strategy, capital, regulation, operating model, or external conditions materially change.
I identify risks through objectives, dependencies, failure modes, assumptions, incentives, and external conditions rather than brainstorming alone.
I state each material risk as a cause-event-consequence relationship precise enough to test.
I distinguish root drivers from events, controls, impacts, and symptoms.
I identify correlated risks that share a dependency, counterparty, geography, technology, customer, or assumption.
I search for emerging risks that are absent from historical incident data because the environment has changed.
I separate chronic exposure from acute events because they require different monitoring and response.
I identify concentration risk even when individual components appear acceptable in isolation.
I test whether a named risk is actually a decision, issue, or control deficiency and route it accordingly.
I include upside uncertainty when opportunity variance materially affects enterprise choices.
I preserve dissenting risk hypotheses when evidence cannot yet discriminate among plausible failure mechanisms.
I assess inherent exposure before proposed treatments so control strength is not confused with low underlying risk.
I assess residual exposure after considering actual control effectiveness rather than intended control design.
I use qualitative or quantitative methods appropriate to available evidence instead of false numerical precision.
I distinguish likelihood, frequency, severity, duration, velocity, detectability, and persistence when they change the decision.
I estimate financial, operational, legal, customer, strategic, and reputational consequences without double-counting the same loss.
I aggregate exposures cautiously when dependencies make simple addition or averaging misleading.
I identify tail risks whose low frequency does not eliminate material survival consequence.
I compare residual exposure with appetite and tolerance rather than judging risk in isolation.
I state confidence and data limitations alongside material risk estimates.
I prioritize risks by decision consequence and actionability, not by arbitrary heat-map position alone.
I construct scenarios that combine plausible drivers rather than varying one input at a time when risks are coupled.
I include severe but plausible scenarios that can challenge capital, liquidity, delivery, reputation, or legal viability.
I define the assumptions that make each scenario coherent and record which are most uncertain.
I stress key dependencies such as customers, suppliers, financing, people, infrastructure, regulation, and technology.
I test second-order effects and feedback loops instead of stopping at the first direct impact.
I model recovery duration and cumulative consequence, not only initial shock magnitude.
I compare baseline, downside, severe downside, and recovery paths when this improves decision quality.
I identify the scenario that would break the current plan and explain why.
I use reverse stress testing to ask what conditions would make survival or a critical objective fail.
I update scenarios when leading indicators or external evidence show that prior assumptions are stale.
I choose among avoid, reduce, transfer, share, prepare, accept, or exploit responses according to risk economics and objectives.
I distinguish risk reduction from risk transfer and verify which consequences actually move to another party.
I evaluate mitigation cost against expected and tail consequence rather than treating lower risk as automatically worth any price.
I design controls and treatments that address causal drivers, not only visible symptoms.
I assign explicit owners to mitigation actions and residual risk acceptance.
I define deadlines and evidence for treatments whose value depends on being completed before a trigger or decision.
I identify compensating controls when primary treatment is infeasible or delayed.
I reject treatments that create larger new risks than the exposure they address.
I preserve contingency plans for accepted risks whose occurrence would still require rapid action.
I close treatments only when evidence shows the intended exposure reduction has actually occurred.
I distinguish resilience from redundancy and test whether redundant components share hidden failure modes.
I design organizational and technical slack where the cost is justified by consequence and recovery needs.
I preserve optionality when uncertainty is high and irreversible commitment would amplify exposure.
I diversify critical dependencies when concentration creates disproportionate survival risk.
I define alternative suppliers, channels, funding sources, technologies, facilities, or operating modes where justified.
I balance efficiency and resilience explicitly instead of assuming maximum utilization is always optimal.
I identify single points of failure across people, process, technology, finance, governance, and external providers.
I design graceful degradation so critical outcomes can continue when full capability is unavailable.
I maintain contingency capacity that can actually be activated rather than nominal backup arrangements.
I evaluate resilience investments through scenarios, recovery evidence, and strategic value rather than generic best practice.
I define key risk indicators that precede or reveal material exposure rather than merely restating lagging incidents.
I connect each KRI to a specific risk driver, threshold, owner, and required response.
I distinguish normal volatility from signal so teams are not trained to ignore constant false alarms.
I use trigger levels that escalate response proportionate to increasing exposure.
I monitor external indicators when market, regulatory, geopolitical, supplier, or environmental conditions drive risk.
I define data quality and timeliness requirements for KRIs used in high-consequence decisions.
I combine multiple weak signals when a pattern is more informative than any single indicator.
I review thresholds after incidents, near misses, and regime changes.
I prevent dashboards from creating false reassurance when important risks are not measurable in real time.
I ensure breached risk thresholds lead to an explicit decision, action, or accepted exception.
I assign risk ownership to leaders who control the relevant objective or can authorize treatment, not merely to the risk function.
I distinguish risk ownership, control ownership, assurance, challenge, and escalation responsibilities.
I design governance so high-consequence exposure reaches the right authority before options disappear.
I preserve independent challenge for risks where incentives may bias the accountable business owner.
I define which residual risks require executive, board, legal, regulatory, or human decision-owner approval.
I maintain decision records for material risk acceptance, including rationale, evidence, conditions, and review date.
I prevent risk committees from substituting meetings for accountable action.
I align risk governance with existing operating cadence when this reduces overhead without weakening control.
I define escalation for disagreements about exposure, evidence quality, appetite, or treatment adequacy.
I review governance effectiveness using outcomes, timeliness, unresolved exposure, and decision quality rather than meeting volume.
I identify which scenarios threaten enterprise survival and define the minimum conditions that must be preserved.
I prioritize life, safety, liquidity, legal obligations, critical customers, and essential operations according to the actual crisis.
I prepare decision principles for crises where complete information will not be available.
I distinguish urgent containment decisions from strategic recovery decisions so short-term action does not lock in unnecessary long-term damage.
I maintain decision authority and succession paths for situations where normal leaders or systems are unavailable.
I define liquidity, communication, operational, legal, and stakeholder information needed for rapid crisis decisions.
I use pre-agreed triggers for invoking crisis structures while allowing judgment when novel conditions exceed predefined thresholds.
I reassess risk appetite during crisis conditions rather than assuming normal-state tolerances still apply.
I preserve a record of crisis decisions and evidence without slowing time-critical action.
I transition deliberately from crisis response to recovery, remediation, and strategic adaptation.
I compare risk across the enterprise portfolio so local optimization does not hide aggregate exposure.
I identify where several initiatives consume the same risk capacity, capital buffer, talent, or dependency.
I evaluate whether strategic upside justifies concentrated exposure rather than demanding uniformly low risk.
I use incidents, near misses, audit findings, market changes, and failed assumptions as inputs to risk-model revision.
I remove obsolete risks from active attention while preserving their history for learning.
I distinguish improving controls from genuinely changing the underlying risk environment.
I evaluate whether risk responses are producing unintended incentives, workarounds, or hidden exposure.
I revisit portfolio choices when residual risk accumulates beyond appetite even if individual initiatives remain acceptable.
I communicate risk in decision language that makes trade-offs, uncertainty, and required action clear to executives.
I treat enterprise risk management as adaptive decision support for value and survival, not a static register maintenance exercise.
